Best Local AI Models for RTX 5090 (32GB)

The RTX 5090 pairs 32GB of GDDR7 with 1,792 GB/s of bandwidth, the most of any consumer card. It runs 8B models at est. 213 tok/s, typical error 5% and dense 32B models at est. 70 tok/s, fully in VRAM. A 70B model does not fit at Q4 and spills into system RAM.

Last updated: November 9, 2026 · Editor: ModelFit Team

Compare with another device
Quick answer

The best local LLM for the RTX 5090 is Qwen3.8 27B (est. 89 tok/s, typical error 5%) on its 32GB VRAM. It uses ~16.5GB of VRAM; the RTX 5090 handles dense models up to ~33B at Q4. A 32B model at Q4 runs at est. 70 tok/s, typical error 5%. (ModelFit, 2026)

Sizing rule: a Q4 model needs about 0.6 GB of VRAM per billion parameters for its weights, and ModelFit budgets 90% of this card's 32GB (28.8GB) for weights, context, and KV-cache. Real files often load more than that rule, so the per-size table below checks actual builds: a size fits only when the lightest Q4 build of that size in our catalog loads within 28.8GB. MoE rows, and sizes with no such build, use a typical Q4 file size. Other strong fits: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (35B, ~22GB) and Sage-A1.5 (35.95B, ~21.7GB). On this card Qwen3.8 27B runs at est. 89 tok/s, typical error 5%. What it will not run: a 70B model does not fit in VRAM alone, so it spills to system RAM over PCIe and slows sharply.

$ollama run qwen3.8:27b

ModelFit estimates, not measured benchmarks: decode speed of a generic Q4_K_M model of each size at 4K context on the RTX 5090's 1792 GB/s bandwidth. MoE rows scale by active parameters (decode reads only the active experts), so a 35B MoE runs far faster than a dense 32B. "CPU offload" sizes exceed the 32GB VRAM; dense models slow to a crawl there, MoE models degrade less because hot experts stay GPU-resident. Offload rows are rough estimates: no measured run covers offload, so they carry no typical error. What typical error means.

Fig. 2

Context costs VRAM too.

Qwen3.8 27B loads ~16.5 GB of weights; at 16k context the KV cache adds ~1.0 GB (still fits the ~29 GB usable VRAM), and at 64k it adds ~4.0 GB (still fits).

Weights 17 GBKV cache · 16k context 1.0 GBHeadroom 11 GBRuntime reserve 3.2 GB

The model leaves about 11 GB of the usable VRAM budget free after weights and 16k context.

KV-cache figures assume an fp16 cache, the llama.cpp/Ollama default. Standard GQA models use a size-class estimate (8 KV heads x 128 head dim class); hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3.5/3.6, Qwen3-Next) use the exact per-token cost from their published config, since only their sparse full-attention layers cache KV. A q8_0 KV cache roughly halves either figure. Estimates, not measurements.

RTX 5090 VRAM for AI: what actually fits?

32GB GDDR7 at 1,792 GB/s is the highest bandwidth of any consumer card. ModelFit budgets about 28.8GB of it for weights and context, which holds dense models up to 33B at Q4 and 35B-class mixture-of-experts models at est. 298 tok/s, typical error 15%. The 5090 also handles multi-model setups: run a 14B chat model alongside a 7B coding model simultaneously. A 70B model at Q4 needs more than that budget, so part of it sits in system RAM, where the estimate falls to est. 3 tok/s, rough estimate, offload not measured.

RTX 5090 FAQ: common questions

How much VRAM does the RTX 5090 have for LLMs?

The RTX 5090 has 32GB GDDR7 VRAM with 1,792 GB/s bandwidth, the most of any consumer GPU. ModelFit budgets about 28.8GB of it for weights and context, so dense models up to 33B at Q4 fit entirely in VRAM.

What size LLM can I run on an RTX 5090?

Dense models up to 33B at Q4 quantization fit entirely in VRAM, and 35B-class MoE models run at est. 298 tok/s, typical error 15%. For 7B-8B models it delivers est. 213 tok/s, typical error 5% (14B lands around est. 142 tok/s). A 70B model needs CPU offload, where the estimate drops to est. 3 tok/s, rough estimate, offload not measured.

Is the RTX 5090 good for local AI in 2026?

The RTX 5090 has the most VRAM (32GB) and the highest bandwidth (1,792 GB/s) of any consumer GPU. At est. 213 tok/s, typical error 5% on 8B models, responses feel instant. Its 32GB VRAM holds 32B models with more room for context than any 24GB card. The 2026 memory shortage has pushed it far above its $1,999 launch MSRP, so it is only justified if you genuinely need large models.

RTX 5090 vs RTX 4090 for running AI models?

The RTX 5090 is 60% faster on 8B models (est. 213 tok/s, typical error 5% vs est. 133 tok/s) with 33% more VRAM (32 vs 24GB). It also fits 35B-class MoE models entirely in VRAM, where the 4090 spills them into system RAM. The 4090 is discontinued and both now trade well above MSRP, but the 5090 is the clear choice for new purchases in 2026.

Can the RTX 5090 replace cloud AI services?

For many use cases, yes. A 32B model on the 5090 rivals GPT-4 quality for coding and reasoning tasks, running at est. 70 tok/s, typical error 5% at Q4 with low latency and complete privacy. The main gap is context length: cloud models support 128K+ tokens, while a long context's KV cache competes with the weights for the same 32GB.

How fast is a 27B-class model like Qwen3.8 27B on the RTX 5090?

ModelFit estimates a 32B model on the RTX 5090 at Q4_K_M runs at est. 70 tok/s, typical error 5%. The current 27B-class pick in the catalog is Qwen3.8 27B (ollama run qwen3.8:27b).
